tools.description: Guides the agent through setting up and configuring a database backend for a MontRS application.
tools.name: skill_database_setup

workflow.description: Steps to follow for this skill

context_invariants: Database configuration must be in montrs.toml, not hardcoded
Connection strings must not be committed to version control
context_prompts: Which database backend would you like to use? (sqlite, postgres, mysql)
What is the connection URL or path for your database?
skill_meta.name: database-setup
workflow_steps: Check montrs.toml for database configuration section
If no database configured, guide user to add [database] section with backend and URL
Run `cargo add` for the chosen backend driver
Verify connection with TestRuntime

tools.description: Guides the agent through deploying a MontRS application to various targets.
tools.name: skill_deployment

workflow.description: Steps to follow for this skill

context_invariants: Environment variables must be configured via montrs.toml, not hardcoded
Deployment configuration must be documented in the project README
context_prompts: What is your deployment target? (web, desktop, mobile)
Do you have a domain or server ready for deployment?
skill_meta.name: deployment
workflow_steps: Determine deployment target: web (WASM+server), desktop (Tauri), or mobile
For web: build with `montrs build --release`, configure static file serving
For desktop: use Tauri integration with `cargo tauri build`
Verify the deployment with a health check or smoke test
Document the deployment configuration in montrs.toml

tools.description: Guides the agent through setting up haptic feedback for a MontRS application.
tools.name: skill_haptics_setup

workflow.description: Steps to follow for this skill

context_invariants: Always call is_supported() before haptic operations
Use ImpactStyle enum, not raw duration values
Feature-gate platform imports to avoid cross-compilation issues
Pass &HapticsConfig to create_haptics_provider, not a raw HapticsTarget
Use enabled: false in tests to get a NoopHapticsProvider
context_prompts: Which platform target does your app use? (web, desktop, mobile)
Which haptic interactions does the app need? (impact, vibration, selection)
skill_meta.name: haptics-setup
workflow_steps: Check which target the application uses (web, desktop, mobile)
Enable the corresponding feature gate (haptics-web, haptics-desktop, or haptics-mobile)
Create a HapticsProvider using create_haptics_provider(&HapticsConfig { enabled: true, target: ... })
Use config.enabled = false to disable haptics at runtime
Wrap provider in a Plate for dependency injection
Configure HapticsConfig with desired settings
Always call provider.is_supported() before haptic operations
Test with cargo test --features haptics-desktop

tools.description: Guides the agent through writing and running tests for MontRS applications.
tools.name: skill_testing

workflow.description: Steps to follow for this skill

context_invariants: Tests must be deterministic and hermetic
Integration tests must use TestRuntime for in-process execution
E2E tests must be tagged with #[cfg(feature = "e2e")]
context_prompts: What type of test are you writing? (unit, integration, e2e)
What is the expected behavior you want to verify?
skill_meta.name: testing
workflow_steps: Identify the target: unit test, integration test, or E2E test
For unit tests: use the test crate's expect() and table_test() macros
For integration tests: use TestRuntime and Fixture traits
For E2E tests: use playwright-rs with the e2e crate
Run tests with `montrs test` or `cargo test --workspace`
Check test output for failures and iterate
